When we look at wider enshitification patterns being pushed in some industries I can't exactly see AI being a problem for those specific sectors. Similarly I don't see a problem in areas that want to create adversarial customer interactions. At least as long as someone is on the hook to quality control that adversarial relationship in the shareholder's favor. That's the patern I'm unfortunately expecting for developers. Developers on the hook for auditing the AI slop code. People hired entirely to get around to plugging the holes the AI makes. It probably will be a full time job as the AI pushes new features, UI updates, and otherwise opens new bugs. From the outside as someone who isn't playing with AI generated code for work currently it seems like it will be the same kind of problem space as a developer inheriting a legacy codebase. In some ways it will be worse, that AI "developer" probably won't be any more useful than the legacy developer who retired for figuring out "why" something was set up a specific way. It will most likely still be around fiddling with your code though, but if your company is locked in to one model it might be easier to learn to read... at least until they change models and you need to learn the style of the new "developer" you can't fathom.

I have and use both Logic and Ableton Live Suite (which is needed for Max 4 live.) They are both great DAWs, and they can complement each other well. Which one you may prefer comes down to the type of music you create and whether you prefer a traditional linear arrangement style of recording (Logic and Ableton are both strong here, although Logic has a more traditional UI) or a session/live-loops based style of recording (Ableton is much stronger here than Logic IMHO.) If your budget constrains you to Garage Band -> Logic or Ableton Lite -> Standard, you will get more with the upgrade to Logic, especially if you rely on the instruments/presets that come with the DAW rather than 3rd party plugins. Note that you can't use the Scheme integration unless you buy Ableton Live Suite, which costs considerably more than Logic or Standard.

Claude usage limit reset is a gambler's rush I have a humble Pro Claude sub for my personal projects, and I use it on Android. So I used up my weekly limit on Monday, and I was going about my day waiting for Thursday to continue. Then I checked the app for whatever reason and noticed 2 limit resets. 1 for all model usage and 1 for Fable 5.2, and I had the experience of a gambler's rush. "I can do so many things now," I thought and clicked instantly on the reset without thinking, like a gambler's finger on a slot machine. "I won something." So I instantly got the motivation dopamine and got to work, and I was reckless. I instantly set up 2 Fable 5.2 agents to start auditing a codebase and an Opus 5.5 to start doing my todo list. And guess what? I ran out of usage without being productive. Now I have to wait 5 hours for the next reset. The combination of a gambler's rush and sudden motivation causes rushed decision-making. Instead of just setting an audit for overnight or doing my todos, I wanted it all and failed to manage it spectacularly. So that's what I think. Claude is as addictive as a substance or at least like a casio.
